title.zh: 卷一百七十 列傳第五十八 于謙
title.raw: 卷一百七十 列傳第五十八 于謙 Volume 170 Biographies 58: Yu Qian

sentences.zh: 于謙子:冕 附:吳寧 王偉

translations.literal: Yu Qian's son: Mian; appended: Wu Ning, Wang Wei
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian's son Mian; appended biographies: Wu Ning and Wang Wei

sentences.zh: 于謙，字廷益，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Yu Qian, styled Tingyi, was a man of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian, whose style was Tingyi, came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 生七歲，有僧奇之曰：「他日救時宰相也。」

translations.literal: When he was seven years old, a monk marvelled at him and said: "In the future you will be the prime minister who saves the age."
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seven, a monk took him for remarkable and said, "One day you will be the statesman who rescues the realm.

sentences.zh: 舉永樂十九年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the nineteenth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the nineteenth year of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，授御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande, he was appointed supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuande reign he was made a supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 奏對，音吐鴻暢，帝為傾聽。

translations.literal: When he answered in audience, his voice and enunciation were grand and clear, and the emperor listened attentively.
translations.idiomatic: In audience his speech rang clear and resonant, and the emperor listened with rapt attention.

sentences.zh: 顧佐為都御史，待寮屬甚嚴，獨下謙，以為才勝己也。

translations.literal: Gu Zuo was censor-in-chief and treated his subordinates very strictly, but alone treated Qian with deference, considering that Qian's talent surpassed his own.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zuo, the censor-in-chief, was severe with his staff yet showed deference only to Qian, judging Qian's ability to exceed his own.

sentences.zh: 扈蹕樂安，高煦出降，帝命謙口數其罪。

translations.literal: When accompanying the imperial procession to Le'an, Gaoxu came out to surrender, and the emperor ordered Qian to recite his crimes aloud.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign to Le'an, Zhu Gaoxu came out to surrender, and the emperor ordered Qian to enumerate his crimes aloud.

sentences.zh: 謙正詞嶄嶄，聲色震厲。

translations.literal: Qian's righteous words were sharp and cutting, his voice and bearing awe-inspiring.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's righteous words cut like a blade; his voice and bearing were fierce and imposing.

sentences.zh: 高煦伏地戰慄，稱萬死。

translations.literal: Gaoxu prostrated himself trembling and said he deserved ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoxu prostrated himself, trembling, and declared himself deserving of death ten thousand times over.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 師還，賞賚與諸大臣等。

translations.literal: When the army returned, rewards and gifts were equal to those of the other grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, his rewards matched those of the other chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 出按江西，雪冤囚數百。

translations.literal: He went out on inspection to Jiangxi and cleared the injustice of several hundred prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to inspect Jiangxi, he righted the wrongful imprisonment of several hundred people.

sentences.zh: 疏奏陝西諸處官校為民害，詔遣御史捕之。

translations.literal: He memorialized that official runners in various places in Shaanxi were harming the people, and an edict dispatched censors to arrest them.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that official runners across Shaanxi were preying on the people, and an edict sent censors to seize them.

sentences.zh: 帝知謙可大任，會增設各部右侍郎為直省巡撫，乃手書謙名授吏部，超遷兵部右侍郎，巡撫河南、山西。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Qian could be entrusted with great responsibility; as they were adding vice ministers in each ministry as grand coordinators for the provinces, he personally wrote Qian's name and gave it to the Ministry of Personnel, promoting him in extraordinary fashion to Vice Minister of War with grand coordination over Henan and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw that Qian was fit for heavy responsibility. As new vice-ministerial posts were created in each ministry to serve as provincial grand coordinators, he wrote Qian's name by hand and sent it to the Ministry of Personnel, promoting him directly to Vice Minister of War with grand coordination over Henan and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 謙至官，輕騎遍曆所部，延訪父老，察時事所宜興革，即俱疏言之。

translations.literal: When Qian arrived at his post, he rode light cavalry throughout his jurisdiction, consulting elderly locals and investigating what should be instituted or abolished according to the times, and memorialized on all of it at once.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Qian rode light cavalry through his entire jurisdiction, seeking out elders and assessing what the times required to be changed or kept, then memorialized on everything together.

sentences.zh: 一歲凡數上，小有水旱，輒上聞。

translations.literal: Within one year he submitted several times; if there was even a minor flood or drought, he reported it immediately.
translations.idiomatic: In a single year he submitted several memorials; even a minor flood or drought he reported at once.

sentences.zh: 正統六年疏言：「今河南、山西積谷各數百萬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong he memorialized saying: "Today Henan and Shanxi each have accumulated grain of several million.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhengtong he memorialized: "Henan and Shanxi now each hold grain reserves of several million bushels.

sentences.zh: 請以每歲三月，令府州縣報缺食下戶，隨分支給。

translations.literal: I request that each year in the third month the prefectures, departments, and counties report households short of food among the lower ranks, and grain be distributed to them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Each March, let prefectures, departments, and counties report households among the poor that lack food, and issue grain to them in turn.

sentences.zh: 先菽秫，次黍麥，次稻。

translations.literal: First beans and broomcorn millet, next panicled millet and wheat, next rice.
translations.idiomatic: Issue beans and broomcorn millet first, then panicled millet and wheat, then rice.

sentences.zh: 俟秋成償官，而免其老疾及貧不能償者。

translations.literal: Wait until the autumn harvest to repay the government, and exempt the aged, ill, and poor who cannot repay.
translations.idiomatic: Let repayment to the state wait until the autumn harvest, and exempt the elderly, the sick, and the destitute who cannot repay.

sentences.zh: 州縣吏秩滿當遷，預備糧有未足，不聽離任。

translations.literal: When prefectural and county officials' terms expired and they were due for transfer, if reserve grain was not yet sufficient they were not permitted to leave their posts.
translations.idiomatic: When prefectural and county officials completed their terms, they should not be allowed to depart if reserve grain still fell short.

sentences.zh: 仍令風憲官以時稽察。」

translations.literal: Still order the surveillance officials to inspect on schedule."
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance officials should also conduct periodic inspections."

sentences.zh: 詔行之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered these measures carried out.

sentences.zh: 河南近河處，時有沖決。

translations.literal: In Henan near rivers, breaches often occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Along Henan's rivers, dikes were breached again and again.

sentences.zh: 謙令厚築堤障，計裏置亭，亭有長，責以督率修繕。

translations.literal: Qian ordered substantial dike construction, setting up pavilions every li with a chief responsible for supervising repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qian ordered heavy reinforcement of the dikes, placing a watch pavilion every li, each with a chief charged to supervise repairs.

sentences.zh: 並令種樹鑿井，榆柳夾路，道無渴者。

translations.literal: He also ordered trees planted and wells dug; elm and willow lined the roads so that travelers on the road had none thirsty.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered trees planted and wells sunk; elms and willows lined the highways so no traveler went thirsty.

sentences.zh: 大同孤懸塞外，按山西者不及至，奏別設御史治之。

translations.literal: Datong stood alone beyond the frontier pass; the Shanxi inspector could not reach it, so he memorialized to establish a separate censor to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: Datong lay isolated beyond the frontier, beyond the reach of the Shanxi inspector; he memorialized to appoint a separate censor to govern it.

sentences.zh: 盡奪鎮將私墾田為官屯，以資邊用。

translations.literal: He confiscated all the frontier generals' privately reclaimed fields and made them official military colonies to fund border expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He seized all privately reclaimed land held by frontier generals and converted it to official military colonies to support border expenditures.

sentences.zh: 威惠流行，太行伏盜皆避匿。

translations.literal: His authority and benevolence spread abroad; hidden bandits in the Taihang ranges all went into concealment.
translations.idiomatic: His authority and kindness spread through the region, and brigands hiding in the Taihang Mountains all went to ground.

sentences.zh: 在官九年，遷左侍郎，食二品俸。

translations.literal: After nine years in office he was transferred to Left Vice Minister with second-rank salary.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years in office he was promoted to Left Vice Minister with second-rank emolument.

sentences.zh: 初，三楊在政府，雅重謙。

translations.literal: Initially the Three Yangs were in government and held Qian in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the Three Yangs held power, they greatly valued Qian.

sentences.zh: 謙所奏，朝上夕報可，皆三楊主持。

translations.literal: Whatever Qian submitted was approved by morning or evening, all through the Three Yangs' sponsorship.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Qian memorialized was approved the same day, always with the Three Yangs behind it.

sentences.zh: 而謙每議事京師，空橐以入，諸權貴人不能無望。

translations.literal: Yet whenever Qian came to the capital on business he entered with empty purses, and the powerful could not be without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever Qian came to the capital on business he arrived with empty pockets, and the powerful could not help but resent him.

sentences.zh: 及是，三楊已前卒，太監王振方用事。

translations.literal: By this time the Three Yangs had all died earlier, and the eunuch Wang Zhen was wielding power.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Three Yangs had all died, and the eunuch Wang Zhen held sway.

sentences.zh: 適有御史姓名類謙者，嘗忤振。

translations.literal: There happened to be a censor whose name resembled Qian's who had once offended Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: There happened to be another censor whose name resembled Qian's and who had once crossed Zhen.

sentences.zh: 謙入朝，薦參政王來、孫原貞自代。

translations.literal: When Qian entered court he recommended Administrating Vice Commissioners Wang Lai and Sun Yuanzhen to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: On entering court Qian recommended the administrating vice commissioners Wang Lai and Sun Yuanzhen to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 通政使李錫阿振指，劾謙以久不遷怨望，擅舉人自代。

translations.literal: Chief of Transmission Li Xi toadied to Zhen's intent and impeached Qian for nursing resentment over long failure to transfer and for presumptuously recommending others to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi, chief of the Office of Transmission, curried favor with Zhen and impeached Qian for resenting his long stagnation and for presumptuously naming his own replacement.

sentences.zh: 下法司論死，繫獄三月。

translations.literal: He was sent to the judicial offices for sentence of death and imprisoned three months.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the judicial offices for a death sentence, and he was imprisoned for three months.

sentences.zh: 已而振知其誤，得釋，左遷大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: Eventually Zhen learned of the error; Qian was released and demoted to Vice Director of the Court of Revision.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen eventually learned of the mistake; Qian was released but demoted to vice director of the Court of Revision.

sentences.zh: 山西、河南吏民伏闕上書，請留謙者以千數，周、晉諸王亦言之，乃復命謙巡撫。

translations.literal: Officials and commoners of Shanxi and Henan knelt at the palace gate submitting memorials; those asking to retain Qian numbered in the thousands, and the Zhou and Jin princes also spoke, whereupon Qian was again ordered to grand coordination.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners of Shanxi and Henan knelt at the palace gate in thousands to beg that Qian stay; the Zhou and Jin princes spoke as well, and Qian was restored to his grand coordination post.

sentences.zh: 時山東、陝西流民就食河南者二十余萬，謙請發河南、懷慶二府積粟以振。

translations.literal: At the time over two hundred thousand refugees from Shandong and Shaanxi had come to Henan seeking food; Qian requested that accumulated grain in the two prefectures of Henan and Huaqing be released for relief.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred thousand refugees from Shandong and Shaanxi had fled to Henan for food; Qian asked that grain reserves in Henan and Huaqing prefectures be opened for relief.

sentences.zh: 又奏令布政使年富安集其眾，授田給牛種，使裏老司察之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized ordering the provincial administration commissioner Nian Fu to settle the multitude, grant fields and provide oxen and seed, and have village elders supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that the provincial administration commissioner Nian Fu should settle the refugees, assign fields, and provide oxen and seed, with village elders to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 前後在任十九年，丁內外艱，皆令歸治喪，旋起復。

translations.literal: Altogether he was in office nineteen years; when he encountered mourning for father or mother he was each time ordered to return and observe the funeral rites, then soon recalled to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: In all he served nineteen years; when mourning fell upon him for father or mother he was sent home to observe the rites, then promptly recalled.

sentences.zh: 十三年以兵部左侍郎召。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was summoned as Left Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was recalled as Left Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，也先大入寇，王振挾帝親征。

translations.literal: The next autumn Esen launched a major invasion, and Wang Zhen compelled the emperor to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn Esen invaded in force, and Wang Zhen pressed the emperor to lead the campaign himself.

sentences.zh: 謙與尚書鄺埜極諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Qian and Minister Kuang Ye remonstrated to the utmost, but were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qian and Minister Kuang Ye remonstrated with all their strength, but were not heard.

sentences.zh: 埜從治兵，留謙理部事。

translations.literal: Ye followed to manage the army; Qian was left to handle ministry affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ye went with the army; Qian was left to manage the ministry's affairs.

sentences.zh: 及駕陷土木，京師大震，眾莫知所為。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was trapped at Tumu, the capital was greatly shaken and none knew what to do.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was captured at Tumu, the capital was convulsed with panic and no one knew what to do.

sentences.zh: 郕王監國，命群臣議戰守。

translations.literal: The Prince of Cheng supervised the state and ordered the ministers to deliberate on fighting or holding.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Cheng took charge of the realm and ordered the ministers to debate whether to fight or to hold the capital.

sentences.zh: 侍講徐珵言星象有變，當南遷。

translations.literal: Court Lecturer Xu Xing said the stars showed change and that they should move the capital south.
translations.idiomatic: Court lecturer Xu Xing said the heavens showed ominous signs and urged moving the capital south.

sentences.zh: 謙厲聲曰：「言南遷者，可斬也。

translations.literal: Qian said in a stern voice: "Whoever speaks of moving south may be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian said sharply: "Whoever speaks of moving south deserves death.

sentences.zh: 京師天下根本，一動則大事去矣，獨不見宋南渡事乎！」

translations.literal: The capital is the root of all under Heaven; if it moves then the great affair is lost—have you alone not seen the affair of the Song moving south across the river!"
translations.idiomatic: The capital is the foundation of the realm; move it and the cause is lost—have you forgotten how the Song fled south across the Yangzi!"

sentences.zh: 王是其言，守議乃定。

translations.literal: The prince approved his words, and the plan to hold was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The prince agreed, and the decision to defend the capital was settled.

sentences.zh: 時京師勁甲精騎皆陷沒，所餘疲卒不及十萬，人心震恐，上下無固志。

translations.literal: At the time the capital's strong armor and elite cavalry had all been lost; the remaining weary soldiers did not reach one hundred thousand, hearts were shaken with terror, and above and below had no firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's best armor and cavalry had perished; fewer than a hundred thousand exhausted troops remained. Panic gripped every heart, and court and city alike lacked firm resolve.

sentences.zh: 謙請王檄取兩京、河南備操軍，山東及南京沿海備倭軍，江北及北京諸府運糧軍，亟赴京師。

translations.literal: Qian requested the prince issue orders to summon the training armies of the Two Capitals and Henan, the coastal anti-Wokou armies of Shandong and Nanjing, and the grain-transport armies of Jiangbei and the various prefectures of Beijing, to hurry to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Qian asked the prince to issue orders summoning training troops from the two capitals and Henan, coastal anti-pirate forces from Shandong and Nanjing, and grain-transport troops from Jiangbei and the Beijing prefectures—all to rush to the capital.

sentences.zh: 以次經畫部署，人心稍安。

translations.literal: He deployed them in sequence step by step, and hearts were somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged deployments in orderly stages, and minds grew somewhat steadier.

sentences.zh: 即遷本部尚書。

translations.literal: He was immediately transferred to Minister of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promptly promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 郕王方攝朝，廷臣請族誅王振。

translations.literal: The Prince of Cheng was just regent in court; court ministers requested extermination of Wang Zhen's entire clan.
translations.idiomatic: As the Prince of Cheng held court, ministers called for the extermination of Wang Zhen's entire clan.

sentences.zh: 而振党馬順者，輒叱言官。

translations.literal: But Wang Zhen's partisan Ma Shun shouted down the remonstrating officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen's follower Ma Shun shouted down the remonstrating officials.

sentences.zh: 於是給事中王竑廷擊順，眾隨之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Supervising Secretary Wang Hong struck Shun in the court, and the multitude followed.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wang Hong then struck Shun in open court, and the crowd followed.

sentences.zh: 朝班大亂，衛卒聲洶洶。

translations.literal: The court ranks fell into great disorder, and the guard soldiers' voices were turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: The court ranks dissolved into chaos; the guards' shouts rose in a roar.

sentences.zh: 王懼欲起，謙排眾直前掖王止，且啟王宣諭曰：「順等罪當死，勿論。」

translations.literal: The prince in fear wished to rise; Qian pushed through the crowd straight forward to support the prince and stop him, and also addressed the prince to proclaim saying: "Shun and the rest deserve death by law—do not discuss it."
translations.idiomatic: The prince, frightened, tried to rise; Qian pushed through the throng, seized the prince's arm, and urged him to announce: "Shun and his like deserve death—let it pass."

sentences.zh: 眾乃定。

translations.literal: The multitude then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the crowd quiet.

sentences.zh: 謙袍袖為之盡裂。

translations.literal: Qian's robe sleeves were completely torn because of it.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's sleeves were torn to shreds in the crush.

sentences.zh: 退出左掖門，吏部尚書王直執謙手歎曰「國家正賴公耳。

translations.literal: Exiting the Left Flank Gate, Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi grasped Qian's hand and sighed: "The state just now relies on you.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving by the Left Flank Gate, Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi took Qian's hand and sighed: "The realm now depends on you alone.

sentences.zh: 今日雖百王直何能為！」

translations.literal: Today even a hundred Wang Zhis—what could they do!"
translations.idiomatic: Today a hundred men like me could do nothing!"

sentences.zh: 當是時，上下皆倚重謙，謙亦毅然以社稷安危為己任。

translations.literal: At that time above and below all relied on Qian, and Qian also resolutely took the security of state and altars as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment court and capital alike leaned on Qian, and Qian in turn took the fate of the realm upon himself without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 初，大臣憂國無主，太子方幼，寇且至，請皇太后立郕王。

translations.literal: Initially the grand ministers worried the state had no ruler, the heir apparent was still young, and the enemy was about to arrive; they requested the empress dowager install the Prince of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, ministers feared the realm had no ruler: the heir was young, the enemy was near, and they asked the empress dowager to enthrone the Prince of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 王驚謝至再。

translations.literal: The prince in alarm declined repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, alarmed, declined again and again.

sentences.zh: 謙揚言曰：「臣等誠憂國家，非為私計。」

translations.literal: Qian proclaimed aloud: "We ministers truly worry for the state and altars, not for private calculation."
translations.idiomatic: Qian declared aloud: "We act only from concern for the state, not from private ambition."

sentences.zh: 王乃受命。

translations.literal: The prince then accepted the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then accepted.

sentences.zh: 九月，景帝立，謙入對，慷慨泣奏曰：「寇得志，要留大駕，勢必輕中國，長驅而南。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Jing Emperor was established; Qian entered audience and, moved with emotion, wept as he memorialized: "The enemy has gained its aim and will detain the great carriage; they are certain to slight China and drive south at length.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Jing Emperor was enthroned. Qian came before him, weeping as he spoke: "The enemy has triumphed and will hold the emperor hostage; they will surely despise China and drive south in force.

sentences.zh: 請飭諸邊守臣協力防遏。

translations.literal: I request that frontier guarding ministers on all sides be ordered to cooperate in defense and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Order every frontier commander to cooperate in defense.

sentences.zh: 京營兵械且盡，宜亟分道募民兵，令工部繕器甲。

translations.literal: The capital garrison's weapons and armor are nearly exhausted; we should urgently recruit civilian soldiers by separate routes and order the Ministry of Works to repair weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: The capital garrison's arms are nearly gone—recruit militia at once along several routes, and have the Ministry of Works repair armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 遣都督孫鏜、衛穎、張軏、張儀、雷通分兵守九門要地，列營郭外。

translations.literal: Dispatch Military Commissioners Sun Tang, Wei Ying, Zhang Yuan, Zhang Yi, and Lei Tong to divide troops and guard the nine gates' vital points, arraying camps outside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Send the military commissioners Sun Tang, Wei Ying, Zhang Yuan, Zhang Yi, and Lei Tong to hold the nine gates' critical points with divided forces, and pitch camps outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 都御史楊善、給事中王竑參之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Yang Shan and Supervising Secretary Wang Hong should assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Let Censor-in-chief Yang Shan and supervising secretary Wang Hong assist them.

sentences.zh: 徙附郭居民入城。

translations.literal: Move suburban residents into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Move residents from the suburbs inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 通州積糧，令官軍自詣關支，以贏米為之直，毋棄以資敵。

translations.literal: For accumulated grain at Tongzhou, order officers and soldiers to go in person to the pass to draw it, taking surplus rice as payment in kind, and not abandoning it to supply the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: For grain stored at Tongzhou, let troops draw it themselves at the passes, paying with surplus rice so nothing is abandoned to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 文臣如軒輗者，宜用為巡撫。

translations.literal: Civil officials such as Xuan Ni should be employed as grand coordinators.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials such as Xuan Ni should serve as grand coordinators.

sentences.zh: 武臣如石亨、楊洪、柳溥者，宜用為將帥。

translations.literal: Military officials such as Shi Heng, Yang Hong, and Liu Pu should be employed as generals.
translations.idiomatic: Military men such as Shi Heng, Yang Hong, and Liu Pu should serve as commanders.

sentences.zh: 至軍旅之事，臣身當之，不效則治臣罪。」

translations.literal: As for military affairs, I myself will undertake them; if ineffective then punish my crime."
translations.idiomatic: As for the conduct of war, I will answer for it myself—if I fail, punish me."

sentences.zh: 帝深納之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 十月敕謙提督各營軍馬。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict ordered Qian to supervise all camps' armies and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an edict placed Qian in overall command of all camp forces.

sentences.zh: 而也先挾上皇破紫荊關直入，窺京師。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Esen, holding the former emperor, broke through Zijing Pass and entered directly, spying on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Esen, holding the captive emperor, broke through Zijing Pass and pressed toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 石亨議斂兵堅壁老之。

translations.literal: Shi Heng proposed gathering troops, strengthening walls, and wearing the enemy down.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng urged pulling troops inside the walls and waiting the enemy out.

sentences.zh: 謙不可，曰：「奈何示弱，使敵益輕我。」

translations.literal: Qian would not agree and said: "How can we show weakness and make the enemy further slight us."
translations.idiomatic: Qian refused: "How can we show weakness and invite the enemy to despise us further?"

sentences.zh: 亟分遣諸將，率師二十二萬，列陣九門外：都督陶瑾安定門，廣寧伯劉安東直門，武進伯硃瑛朝陽門，都督劉聚西直門，鎮遠侯顧興祖阜成門，都指揮李端正陽門，都督劉得新崇文門，都指揮湯節宣武門，而謙自與石亨率副總兵范廣、武興陳德勝門外，當也先。

translations.literal: He urgently dispatched the various generals, leading an army of two hundred twenty thousand and arraying formations outside the nine gates: Military Commissioner Tao Jin at Anding Gate, Earl of Guangning Liu An at Dongzhi Gate, Baron of Wujin Zhu Ying at Chaoyang Gate, Military Commissioner Liu Ju at Xizhi Gate, Marquis of Zhenyuan Gu Xingzu at Fucheng Gate, Regional Commander Li Duan at Zhengyang Gate, Military Commissioner Liu Dexin at Chongwen Gate, Regional Commander Tang Jie at Xuanwu Gate, while Qian himself with Shi Heng led Vice Commanders-in-chief Fan Guang and Wu Xing Chen De outside Desheng Gate to face Esen.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent out his generals with two hundred twenty thousand men, drawing up battle lines outside the nine gates: Tao Jin at Anding, Liu An at Dongzhi, Zhu Ying at Chaoyang, Liu Ju at Xizhi, Gu Xingzu at Fucheng, Li Duan at Zhengyang, Liu Dexin at Chongwen, Tang Jie at Xuanwu—while Qian himself, with Shi Heng, Fan Guang, and Chen De, took position outside Desheng Gate to meet Esen head-on.

sentences.zh: 以部事付侍郎吳寧，悉閉諸城門，身自督戰。

translations.literal: He entrusted ministry affairs to Vice Minister Wu Ning, closed all city gates completely, and personally supervised the battle.
translations.idiomatic: He left ministry affairs to Vice Minister Wu Ning, shut every gate, and supervised the fighting in person.

sentences.zh: 下令，臨陣將不顧軍先退者，斬其將。

translations.literal: He issued orders: in battle if a general does not care for the army and retreats first, execute the general.
translations.idiomatic: He issued orders: any general who retreats before his men will be executed.

sentences.zh: 軍不顧將先退者，後隊斬前隊。

translations.literal: If soldiers do not care for the general and retreat first, the rear rank executes the front rank.
translations.idiomatic: Any soldier who retreats before his commander will be cut down by the rank behind.

sentences.zh: 於是將士知必死，皆用命。

translations.literal: Thereupon officers and soldiers knew they must die and all obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men knew they faced certain death, and all fought as ordered.

sentences.zh: 副總兵高禮、毛福壽卻敵彰義門北，擒其長一人。

translations.literal: Vice Commanders-in-chief Gao Li and Mao Fushou repelled the enemy north of Zhangyi Gate and captured one of their chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commanders Gao Li and Mao Fushou drove the enemy back north of Zhangyi Gate and captured one of their leaders.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，令謙選精兵屯教場以便調用，復命太監興安、李永昌同謙理軍務。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and ordered Qian to select elite troops stationed on the drill ground for convenient deployment, and again ordered eunuchs Xing'an and Li Yongchang to handle military affairs together with Qian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and ordered Qian to select elite troops and hold them on the drill ground for rapid deployment; eunuchs Xing'an and Li Yongchang were again assigned to assist Qian in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，也先深入，視京城可旦夕下。

translations.literal: Initially Esen had penetrated deeply and regarded the capital as fallible within a morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: At first Esen had driven deep inland, expecting to take the capital within a day.

sentences.zh: 及見官軍嚴陣待，意稍沮。

translations.literal: When he saw the government army in strict formation waiting, his intent was somewhat discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw government troops drawn up in tight formation awaiting him, his confidence faltered.

sentences.zh: 叛閹喜寧嗾使邀大臣迎駕，索金帛以萬萬計，復邀謙及王直、胡濙等出議。

translations.literal: The rebel eunuch Xi Ning instigated them to invite grand ministers to welcome the imperial carriage, demanding gold and silk counted by the tens of thousands, and again invited Qian and Wang Zhi, Hu Ying, and others to come out to negotiate.
translations.idiomatic: The defecting eunuch Xi Ning urged them to summon ministers to welcome the captive emperor, demanding gold and silk by the myriad, and again invited Qian, Wang Zhi, Hu Ying, and others to come out and negotiate.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，也先氣益沮。

translations.literal: The emperor would not permit it, and Esen's spirit was further discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, and Esen's ardor cooled further.

sentences.zh: 庚申，寇窺德勝門。

translations.literal: On gengshen day the invaders spied on Desheng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day the enemy probed Desheng Gate.

sentences.zh: 謙令亨設伏空舍，遣數騎誘敵。

translations.literal: Qian ordered Heng to set ambush in empty houses and sent several horsemen to lure the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had Heng lay ambush in empty buildings and sent a few horsemen to bait the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵以萬騎來薄，副總兵范廣發火器，伏起齊擊之。

translations.literal: The enemy came with ten thousand horsemen to press close; Vice Commander-in-chief Fan Guang discharged firearms, and the ambush rose together to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand enemy horsemen pressed in; Vice Commander Fan Guang fired his guns, and the ambush rose as one to strike them down.

sentences.zh: 也先弟孛羅、平章卯那孩中砲死。

translations.literal: Esen's younger brother Boluo and Pingzhang Onahai were struck by cannon and died.
translations.idiomatic: Esen's brother Boluo and the pingzhang Onahai were killed by cannon fire.

sentences.zh: 寇轉至西直門，都督孫堂禦之，亨亦分兵至，寇引退。

translations.literal: The invaders turned to Xizhi Gate; Military Commissioner Sun Tang defended against them, and Heng also divided troops and arrived, whereupon the invaders withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy shifted to Xizhi Gate; Sun Tang held them off, and Heng arrived with reinforcements, and the invaders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 副總兵武興擊寇彰義門，與都督王敬挫其前鋒。

translations.literal: Vice Commander-in-chief Wu Xing struck the invaders at Zhangyi Gate and with Military Commissioner Wang Jing checked their vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xing attacked the enemy at Zhangyi Gate; Wang Jing joined him and blunted the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 寇且卻，而內官數百騎欲爭功，躍馬競前。

translations.literal: The invaders were about to retreat, but several hundred horsemen of inner eunuchs wished to compete for merit and spurred their horses to race forward.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was on the verge of retreat when several hundred eunuch horsemen, eager for glory, spurred ahead in a reckless charge.

sentences.zh: 陣亂，興被流矢死，寇逐至土城。

translations.literal: The formation fell into disorder; Xing was killed by a stray arrow, and the invaders pursued to the earthen wall.
translations.idiomatic: The formation broke; Xing fell to a stray arrow, and the enemy chased the rout to the earthen wall.

sentences.zh: 居民升屋，號呼投磚石擊寇，嘩聲動天。

translations.literal: Residents climbed onto roofs, shouting and hurling bricks and stones at the invaders; the clamor shook heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Residents climbed to their rooftops, shouting and hurling bricks and stones at the invaders until the din shook the sky.

sentences.zh: 王竑及福壽援至，寇乃卻。

translations.literal: Wang Hong and Fushou's reinforcements arrived, and the invaders then retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong and Mao Fushou arrived with reinforcements, and the enemy finally withdrew.

sentences.zh: 相持五日，也先邀請既不應，戰又不利，知終弗可得志，又聞勤王師且至，恐斷其歸路，遂擁上皇由良鄉西去。

translations.literal: After five days of stalemate, Esen's invitations received no response and battle was again unfavorable; knowing he could never achieve his aim, and hearing that relief armies were about to arrive and fearing his retreat cut off, he then escorted the former emperor west from Liangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: After five days of stalemate, Esen's invitations went unanswered and his battles went ill; seeing he could not prevail, and hearing relief armies were near—fearing his retreat would be cut—he led the captive emperor west from Liangxiang.

sentences.zh: 謙調諸將追擊，至關而還。

translations.literal: Qian deployed the generals in pursuit, returning when they reached the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Qian sent the generals in pursuit, halting at the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 論功，加謙少保，總督軍務。

translations.literal: When merits were discussed, Qian was promoted to Junior Guardian and made overall supervisor of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit Qian was made Junior Guardian with overall command of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 謙曰：「四郊多壘，卿大夫之恥也，敢邀功賞哉！」

translations.literal: Qian said: "When the four suburbs have many enemy ramparts, it is the shame of ministers and grandees—how dare I seek merit and reward!"
translations.idiomatic: Qian said, "When enemies camp at the capital's gates, it is the minister's shame—how dare I claim reward!"

sentences.zh: 固辭，不允。

translations.literal: He firmly declined, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He refused firmly, but the court would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 乃益兵守真、保、涿、易諸府州，請以大臣鎮山西，防寇南侵。

translations.literal: He then increased troops to guard the prefectures of Zhen, Bao, Zhuo, and Yi, and requested that a grand minister garrison Shanxi to guard against the invaders' southward aggression.
translations.idiomatic: He reinforced the garrisons at Zhending, Baoding, Zhuozhou, and Yizhou, and asked that a senior minister hold Shanxi against a southern thrust.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年三月，總兵硃謙奏敵二萬攻圍萬全，敕范廣充總兵官禦之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Jingtai, Commander-in-chief Zhu Qian memorialized that twenty thousand enemies were attacking and besieging Wanquan; an edict ordered Fan Guang to serve as commander-in-chief to defend.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Jingtai 1, Commander Zhu Qian reported twenty thousand enemies besieging Wanquan; Fan Guang was ordered to take command of the defense.

sentences.zh: 已而寇退，謙請即駐兵居庸，寇來則出關剿殺，退則就糧京師。

translations.literal: Soon the invaders retreated; Qian requested troops be stationed immediately at Juyong—when invaders came they would exit the pass to pursue and kill, and when they retreated they would draw grain from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew, Qian proposed stationing troops at Juyong: sally out to fight when the enemy came, fall back on the capital's grain when they retreated.

sentences.zh: 大同參將許貴奏，迤北有三人至鎮，欲朝廷遣使講和。

translations.literal: Datong Vice General Xu Gui memorialized that three men had come to the garrison from the north, wishing the court to dispatch envoys to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gui, vice general at Datong, reported that three men from the north had arrived seeking peace talks with the court.

sentences.zh: 謙曰：「前遣指揮季鐸、嶽謙往，而也先隨入寇。

translations.literal: Qian said: "Previously we dispatched Commanders Ji Duo and Yue Qian, and Esen followed with invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Qian said, "We once sent Commanders Ji Duo and Yue Qian—and Esen invaded right behind them.

sentences.zh: 繼遣通政王復、少卿趙榮，不見上皇而還。

translations.literal: We then sent Chief of Transmission Wang Fu and Junior Director Zhao Rong, and they returned without seeing the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: We then sent Wang Fu and Zhao Rong—they returned without even seeing the captive emperor.

sentences.zh: 和不足恃，明矣。

translations.literal: Peace cannot be relied upon—it is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Peace cannot be trusted. That much is plain.

sentences.zh: 況我與彼不共戴天，理固不可和。

translations.literal: Moreover we and they cannot live under the same sky; by principle harmony is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: We and they cannot live under the same sky; by right there can be no peace.

sentences.zh: 萬一和而彼肆無厭之求，從之則坐敝，不從則生變，勢亦不得和。

translations.literal: If by chance there were peace and they indulged insatiable demands, to agree would leave us exhausted sitting, and not to agree would breed change—by circumstance peace also could not be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we made peace, their demands would know no end; yield and we exhaust ourselves, refuse and war reignites—in either case peace is impossible.

sentences.zh: 貴為介胄臣，而恇怯如此，何以敵愾，法當誅。」

translations.literal: Gui is a minister in armor and helmet, yet so timid and cowardly—how can he face the enemy with shared wrath? By law he should be executed."
translations.idiomatic: A man who wears armor and yet shows such cowardice—how can he fight the enemy? By law he deserves death."

sentences.zh: 移檄切責。

translations.literal: He sent a dispatch sternly rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a stern rebuke by dispatch.

sentences.zh: 自是邊將人人主戰守，無敢言講和者。

translations.literal: From this time frontier generals all advocated fighting and holding, and none dared speak of negotiating peace.
translations.idiomatic: From then on every frontier commander argued for war and defense; none dared speak of peace.

sentences.zh: 初，也先多所要脅，皆以喜寧為謀主。

translations.literal: Initially Esen's many demands and threats all had Xi Ning as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: At first Esen's endless demands and threats all traced to Xi Ning as mastermind.

sentences.zh: 謙密令大同鎮將擒寧，戮之。

translations.literal: Qian secretly ordered the Datong garrison commander to seize Ning and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian secretly ordered the Datong commander to seize Xi Ning and execute him.

sentences.zh: 又計授王偉誘誅間者小田兒。

translations.literal: He also devised a plan and entrusted Wang Wei to lure and kill the agent Xiaotian'er.
translations.idiomatic: He also set Wang Wei to lure and kill the Mongol agent Xiaotian'er.

sentences.zh: 且因諜用間，請特釋忠勇伯把台家，許以封爵，使陰圖之。

translations.literal: Moreover, using spies to employ stratagems, he requested special release of the family of the Loyal and Brave Earl Batai, promising enfeoffment, to have them plot secretly.
translations.idiomatic: Through espionage he arranged the release of Batai's family, promising them titles if they would work against Esen from within.

sentences.zh: 也先始有歸上皇意，遣使通款，京師稍解嚴。

translations.literal: Esen then first had the intent to return the former emperor, sent envoys to open relations, and the capital slightly relaxed its vigilance.
translations.idiomatic: Esen began to consider returning the captive emperor, sent envoys to negotiate, and the capital eased its alert.

sentences.zh: 謙上言：「南京重地，撫輯須人。

translations.literal: Qian memorialized: "Nanjing is a weighty place; pacification and governance require personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Qian memorialized: "Nanjing is a vital post and needs a capable hand.

sentences.zh: 中原多流民，設遇歲荒，嘯聚可虞。

translations.literal: The central plains have many refugees; if famine years should occur, gathering in bands to shout could be feared.
translations.idiomatic: The central plains hold many refugees; in a famine year they might rise in bands.

sentences.zh: 乞敕內外守備及各巡撫加意整飭。

translations.literal: I beg that internal and external garrison commanders and each grand coordinator be ordered to pay special attention to rectification.
translations.idiomatic: Order every garrison commander and grand coordinator to tighten discipline.

sentences.zh: 防患未然，召還所遣召募文武官及鎮守中官在內地者。」

translations.literal: Guard against trouble before it arises, and recall the civil and military officials sent out for recruitment and the eunuch garrison supervisors in the interior."
translations.idiomatic: Guard against trouble before it arises, and recall the recruitment officers and interior eunuch supervisors dispatched to the provinces."

sentences.zh: 于時八月，上皇北狩且一年矣。

translations.literal: At that time it was the eighth month; the former emperor's northern hunt had already been nearly a year.
translations.idiomatic: It was now the eighth month; the captive emperor had been held in the north nearly a year.

sentences.zh: 也先見中國無釁，滋欲乞和，使者頻至，請歸上皇。

translations.literal: Esen saw China had no openings and increasingly wished to beg peace; envoys came frequently requesting return of the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Esen, finding no weakness in China, grew eager for peace; envoys came again and again asking for the emperor's return.

sentences.zh: 大臣王直等議遣使奉迎，帝不悅曰：「朕本不欲登大位，當時見推，實出卿等。」

translations.literal: Grand ministers Wang Zhi and others deliberated dispatching envoys to welcome him; the emperor said displeased: "I originally did not wish to ascend the great throne; when I was then pushed forward, it truly came from you ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi and other ministers proposed sending envoys to welcome him home. The emperor said coldly, "I never wanted this throne; you ministers put me here."

sentences.zh: 謙從容曰：「天位已定，寧復有他，顧理當速奉迎耳。

translations.literal: Qian said calmly: "The heavenly throne is already settled—how could there be another? Only that by principle we ought quickly to welcome him back.
translations.idiomatic: Qian said evenly, "The throne is settled; there can be no other outcome. Still, we ought to bring him home at once.

sentences.zh: 萬一彼果懷詐，我有辭矣。」

translations.literal: If by chance they truly harbor deceit, we have our justification."
translations.idiomatic: If they are deceiving us, we will have grounds to refuse them."

sentences.zh: 帝顧而改容曰：「從汝，從汝。」

translations.literal: The emperor looked and changed expression, saying: "As you say, as you say."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face softened. "Do as you say. Do as you say."

sentences.zh: 先後遣李實、楊善往。

translations.literal: They successively dispatched Li Shi and Yang Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent—first Li Shi, then Yang Shan.

sentences.zh: 卒奉上皇以歸，謙力也。

translations.literal: In the end they brought the former emperor back—it was Qian's effort.
translations.idiomatic: The former emperor came home at last, and it was Qian's doing.

sentences.zh: 上皇既歸，瓦剌復請朝貢。

translations.literal: After the former emperor returned, the Oirats again requested tributary missions.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's return, the Oirats again sought tributary relations.

sentences.zh: 先是，貢使不過百人，正統十三年至三千餘，賞賚不饜，遂入寇。

translations.literal: Previously tribute envoys did not exceed one hundred men; in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong they reached more than three thousand, rewards and gifts were not satisfied, and they then invaded.
translations.idiomatic: Once their missions numbered fewer than a hundred; by Zhengtong 13 they brought three thousand men, and when rewards no longer satisfied them, they invaded.

sentences.zh: 及是又遣使三千來朝，謙請列兵居庸關備不虞。

translations.literal: By this time they again sent three thousand envoys to court; Qian requested troops arrayed at Juyong Pass against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Now they sent three thousand envoys again; Qian asked for troops at Juyong Pass against surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 京師盛陳兵，宴之。

translations.literal: The capital displayed troops in abundance and feasted them.
translations.idiomatic: The capital paraded its forces and held a grand banquet for them.

sentences.zh: 因言和議難恃，條上安邊三策。

translations.literal: He then spoke that peace negotiations were hard to rely on and listed three policies for securing the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that peace could not be trusted and submitted three policies for securing the frontier.

sentences.zh: 請敕大同、宣府、永平、山海、遼東各路總兵官增修備禦。

translations.literal: He requested edicts to the various route commanders-in-chief of Datong, Xuanfu, Yongping, Shanhai, and Liaodong to increase repairs and defenses.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that commanders along the Datong, Xuanfu, Yongping, Shanhai, and Liaodong routes strengthen their defenses.

sentences.zh: 京兵分隸五軍、神機、三千諸營，雖各有總兵，不相統一，請擇精銳十五萬，分十營團操。

translations.literal: Capital troops were divided among the Five Armies, Divine Engine, and Three Thousand camps; though each had a commander-in-chief they were not unified—he requested selecting one hundred fifty thousand elite troops divided into ten camps for group drill.
translations.idiomatic: Capital troops were scattered across the Five Armies, Divine Engine, and Three Thousand camps without unified command; he proposed selecting one hundred fifty thousand elite troops in ten brigades for joint training.

sentences.zh: 團營之制自此始。

translations.literal: The regiment-camp system began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The regiment system dates from this reform.

sentences.zh: 具《兵志》中。

translations.literal: It is fully set out in the Military Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The details appear in the Military Treatise.

sentences.zh: 瓦剌入貢，每攜故所掠人口至。

translations.literal: When the Oirats came on tribute they each time brought populations previously seized.
translations.idiomatic: On each tributary mission the Oirats brought captives taken in earlier raids.

sentences.zh: 謙必奏酬其使，前後贖還累數百人。

translations.literal: Qian always memorialized to reward their envoys; before and after he ransomed back several hundred people in all.
translations.idiomatic: Qian always memorialized to reward the envoys properly; in all he ransomed back several hundred captives.

sentences.zh: 初，永樂中，降人安置近畿者甚眾。

translations.literal: Initially in the Yongle period, surrendered people settled near the capital region were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongle era many surrendered Mongols had been settled near the capital.

sentences.zh: 也先入寇，多為內應。

translations.literal: When Esen invaded, many served as internal collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen invaded, many acted as collaborators within.

sentences.zh: 謙謀散遣之。

translations.literal: Qian planned to disperse and send them away.
translations.idiomatic: Qian planned to disperse them.

sentences.zh: 因西南用兵，每有征行，輒選其精騎，厚資以往，已更遣其妻子，內患以息。

translations.literal: Because of campaigns in the southwest, whenever there was a expedition he would select their elite cavalry, richly supply them to go, and afterward send their wives and children as well; internal trouble thereby ceased.
translations.idiomatic: As campaigns opened in the southwest, he selected their best horsemen for each expedition, paid them well, and eventually sent their families after them—the internal threat subsided.

sentences.zh: 楊洪自獨石入衛，八城悉以委寇。

translations.literal: Yang Hong entered the guard from Dushi, and all eight cities were entirely yielded to the invaders.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Hong withdrew from Dushi to the capital, all eight border forts were abandoned to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 謙使都督孫安以輕騎出龍門關據之，募民屯田，且戰且守，八城遂復。

translations.literal: Qian had Military Commissioner Sun An lead light cavalry out through Longmen Pass to hold them, recruiting civilians for military colonies, fighting while holding, and the eight cities were thereby recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Qian sent Sun An through Longmen Pass with light cavalry to reclaim them, organized civilian farming colonies, and fought while holding until all eight forts were recovered.

sentences.zh: 貴州苗未平，何文淵議罷二司，專設都司，以大將鎮之。

translations.literal: The Guizhou Miao were not yet pacified; He Wenyuan proposed abolishing the two commissions and establishing only a regional command, with a great general to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: With the Guizhou Miao still unrestful, He Wenyuan proposed abolishing the civil and surveillance commissions and garrisoning the region with a regional command and a great general.

sentences.zh: 謙曰：「不設二司，是棄之也。」

translations.literal: Qian said: "Not establishing the two commissions is to abandon it."
translations.idiomatic: Qian said, "Without the two commissions we would be abandoning the province."

sentences.zh: 議乃寢。

translations.literal: The proposal then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 謙以上皇雖還，國恥未雪，會也先與脫脫不花構，請乘間大發兵，身往討之，以復前仇，除邊患。

translations.literal: Qian, because although the former emperor had returned national shame was not washed away, and as Esen and Togto were at odds, requested seizing the opportunity to launch a great army, going in person to campaign against them, to avenge the former wrong and remove frontier trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor had returned, national humiliation remained unavenged; when Esen fell out with Togto, Qian urged a major campaign to wipe out the old score and end the border threat.

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 謙之為兵部也，也先勢方張；

translations.literal: When Qian was at the Ministry of War, Esen's power was just expanding;
translations.idiomatic: While Qian held the Ministry of War, Esen's power was at its height;

sentences.zh: 而福建鄧茂七、浙江葉宗留、廣東黃蕭養各擁眾僭號；

translations.literal: while in Fujian Deng Maoqi, in Zhejiang Ye Zongliu, and in Guangdong Huang Xiaoyang each gathered multitudes and usurped titles;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Maoqi in Fujian, Ye Zongliu in Zhejiang, and Huang Xiaoyang in Guangdong each raised armies and declared themselves rulers;

sentences.zh: 湖廣、貴州、廣西、瑤、僮、苗、僚所至蜂起。

translations.literal: in Huguang, Guizhou, Guangxi, Yao, Zhuang, Miao, and Lao territories they rose everywhere like bees.
translations.idiomatic: and across Huguang, Guizhou, and Guangxi the Yao, Zhuang, Miao, and Lao peoples rose everywhere like swarming bees.

sentences.zh: 前後徵調，皆謙獨運。

translations.literal: Campaigns before and after were all directed by Qian alone.
translations.idiomatic: Every campaign, before and after, Qian directed alone.

sentences.zh: 當軍馬倥傯，變在俄頃，謙目視指屈，口具章奏，悉合機宜。

translations.literal: When armies and horses were in turmoil and change came in a moment, Qian's eyes watched and fingers moved, his mouth prepared memorials—all fitting the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: When armies were in chaos and crises erupted in an instant, Qian's eyes took in everything and his fingers moved; memorials poured from his lips, every one precisely right.

sentences.zh: 僚吏受成，相顧駭服。

translations.literal: Staff officials received his completed orders and looked at one another in awed submission.
translations.idiomatic: His staff received his orders and looked at one another in awed admiration.

sentences.zh: 號令明審，雖勳臣宿將小不中律，即請旨切責。

translations.literal: His orders were clear and exact; even if meritorious ministers and veteran generals slightly failed regulations, he immediately requested imperial instructions to rebuke them sharply.
translations.idiomatic: His orders were clear and exact; even a meritorious veteran who slightly breached discipline was sharply rebuked by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 片紙行萬里外，靡不惕息。

translations.literal: A slip of paper sent ten thousand li away—none failed to tremble and hold their breath.
translations.idiomatic: A slip of paper from his desk reached ten thousand li away, and none who received it failed to tremble.

sentences.zh: 其才略開敏，精神周至，一時無與比。

translations.literal: His talent and strategy were open and keen, his spirit thorough and complete—for a time none could compare.
translations.idiomatic: His talent was keen, his energy inexhaustible—none in his age could match him.

sentences.zh: 至性過人，憂國忘身。

translations.literal: His utmost nature surpassed others; he worried for the state and forgot himself.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was surpassing; he forgot himself in devotion to the state.

sentences.zh: 上皇雖歸，口不言功。

translations.literal: Although the former emperor returned, he did not speak of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor came home, he never spoke of his own merit.

sentences.zh: 東宮既易，命兼宮僚者支二俸。

translations.literal: After the Eastern Palace was changed, those ordered to serve concurrently as palace staff received two salaries.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir was changed, those appointed as palace tutors were granted double salary.

sentences.zh: 諸臣皆辭，謙獨辭至再。

translations.literal: All ministers declined; Qian alone declined twice.
translations.idiomatic: Other ministers declined once; Qian declined twice.

sentences.zh: 自奉儉約，所居僅蔽風雨。

translations.literal: He himself practiced frugality; his dwelling barely sheltered from wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: He lived frugally in a house that barely kept out wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 帝賜第西華門，辭曰：「國家多難，臣子何敢自安。」

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed a mansion at Xihua Gate; he declined saying: "The state has many hardships—how dare a minister seek ease for himself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor offered him a mansion at Xihua Gate; he declined: "The realm is in crisis—how dare a minister seek comfort?"

sentences.zh: 固辭，不允。

translations.literal: He firmly declined, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He refused firmly, but the court would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 乃取前後所賜璽書、袍、錠之屬，悉加封識，歲時一省視而已。

translations.literal: He then took the imperial letters, robes, ingots, and the like bestowed before and after, all added seals and labels, and once a year merely inspected them.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed away every imperial gift—letters, robes, silver ingots—and opened them only once a year to look them over.

sentences.zh: 帝知謙深，所論奏無不從者。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Qian was profound; whatever he memorialized was never not followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew Qian's depth and never refused his counsel.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣使往真定、河間采野菜，直沽造幹魚，謙一言即止。

translations.literal: He once dispatched envoys to Zhending and Hejian to gather wild vegetables and to Zhigu to make dried fish; at one word from Qian it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor sent men to gather wild vegetables in Zhending and Hejian and to make dried fish at Zhigu; a single word from Qian ended it.

sentences.zh: 用一人，必密訪謙。

translations.literal: To employ one man, he always secretly consulted Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Before appointing anyone, the emperor always consulted Qian in secret.

sentences.zh: 謙具實對，無所隱，不避嫌怨。

translations.literal: Qian answered with full truth, hiding nothing, not avoiding resentment from those disliked.
translations.idiomatic: Qian answered truthfully, hiding nothing and sparing no one's feelings.

sentences.zh: 由是諸不任職者皆怨，而用弗如謙者，亦往往嫉之。

translations.literal: Because of this all the incompetent resented him, and those employed who were not Qian's equal also often envied him.
translations.idiomatic: The incompetent resented him; those less capable than he often envied him.

sentences.zh: 比寇初退，都御史羅通即劾謙上功簿不實。

translations.literal: When the invaders had just retreated, Censor-in-chief Luo Tong immediately impeached Qian for falsifying the merit register.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the enemy withdrew, Censor-in-chief Luo Tong impeached Qian for inflating the merit rolls.

sentences.zh: 御史顧躭言謙太專，請六部大事同內閣奏行。

translations.literal: Censor Gu Dan said Qian was too monopolistic and requested that great affairs of the Six Ministries be submitted together with the Grand Secretariat for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Gu Dan said Qian held too much power and asked that major matters of the Six Ministries go through the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 謙據祖制折之，戶部尚書金濂亦疏爭，而言者捃摭不已。

translations.literal: Qian refuted it according to ancestral institutions; Minister of Revenue Jin Lian also memorialized in dispute, yet the speakers kept gathering accusations without end.
translations.idiomatic: Qian rebutted them on precedent; Minister of Revenue Jin Lian also protested, but the critics kept finding new grievances.

sentences.zh: 諸御史以深文彈劾者屢矣，賴景帝破眾議用之，得以盡所設施。

translations.literal: The various censors impeached with harsh legal wording many times; relying on the Jing Emperor breaking collective opinion to employ him, he was able fully to carry out what he planned.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached him repeatedly on technicalities; only because the Jing Emperor overruled them could Qian carry out his plans.

sentences.zh: 謙性故剛，遇事有不如意，輒拊膺歎曰：「此一腔熱血，意灑何地！」

translations.literal: Qian's nature was by nature rigid; when matters did not go as wished he would strike his chest and sigh: "This one cavity of hot blood—where does it intend to be spilled!"
translations.idiomatic: Qian was by nature stern; when things went wrong he would strike his chest and cry, "This heart's hot blood—where shall it be poured!"

sentences.zh: 視諸選耎大臣、勳舊貴戚意頗輕之，憤者益眾。

translations.literal: He regarded the various chosen weak grand ministers and meritorious old noble kin with intent somewhat slighting them; the resentful grew more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He held the timid ministers and the old nobility in thinly veiled contempt, and his enemies multiplied.

sentences.zh: 又始終不主和議，雖上皇實以是得還，不快也。

translations.literal: Moreover he from first to last did not advocate peace talks; although the former emperor in fact thereby was able to return, he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He had never favored peace talks; though the former emperor owed his return to Qian's policy, he was displeased nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 徐珵以議南遷，為謙所斥。

translations.literal: Xu Xing for advocating moving south was rebuked by Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xing, who had urged moving the capital south, had been rebuked by Qian.

sentences.zh: 至是改名有貞，稍稍進用，嘗切齒謙。

translations.literal: By this time he changed his name to Youzhen and was gradually advanced in employment, and once gnashed his teeth at Qian.
translations.idiomatic: By now he had renamed himself Youzhen and was gradually rising; he gnashed his teeth at the mention of Qian.

sentences.zh: 石亨本以失律削職，謙請宥而用之，總兵十營，畏謙不得逞，亦不樂謙。

translations.literal: Shi Heng originally had his office cut for violating regulations; Qian requested pardon and employed him, commanding the ten camps—fearing Qian he could not have his way, and also was not pleased with Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng had been stripped of rank for a military offense; Qian had him pardoned and put in command of the ten camps. He feared Qian and could not have his way, and he disliked Qian besides.

sentences.zh: 德勝之捷，亨功不加謙而得世侯，內愧，乃疏薦謙子冕。

translations.literal: At the victory at Desheng, Heng's merit was not added to Qian's yet he obtained a hereditary marquisate—inwardly ashamed, he then memorialized recommending Qian's son Mian.
translations.idiomatic: At Desheng, Heng won a hereditary marquisate while Qian received no added credit; ashamed, he memorialized recommending Qian's son Mian.

sentences.zh: 詔赴京師，辭，不允。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to proceed to the capital; he declined and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Mian to the capital; he declined but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 謙言：「國家多事，臣子義不得顧私恩。

translations.literal: Qian said: "The state has many affairs; a minister by righteousness cannot consider private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Qian said, "The realm is in crisis; a minister must not put private favor first.

sentences.zh: 且亨位大將，不聞舉一幽隱，拔一行伍微賤，以裨軍國，而獨薦臣子，于公議得乎？

translations.literal: Moreover Heng holds the position of great general—I have not heard him recommend one obscure worthy or promote one humble soldier of the ranks to benefit state and army, yet he alone recommends my son—does this accord with public opinion?
translations.idiomatic: And Heng is a great general—has he ever recommended an obscure worthy or promoted a humble soldier for the good of the army? To recommend only my son—can that satisfy public opinion?

sentences.zh: 臣于軍功，力杜僥倖，決不敢以子濫功。」

translations.literal: Your minister in military merit strives to block opportunism and absolutely dares not let his son usurp merit."
translations.idiomatic: In matters of military merit I have blocked every shortcut; I would never let my son claim credit he did not earn."

sentences.zh: 亨復大恚。

translations.literal: Heng again was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was furious anew.

sentences.zh: 都督張軏以征苗失律，為謙所劾，與內侍曹吉祥等皆素憾謙。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Zhang Yuan for losing regulations in the Miao campaign was impeached by Qian; with inner attendant Cao Jixiang and others they all long resented Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuan had been impeached by Qian for a disciplinary breach in the Miao campaign; he and the eunuch Cao Jixiang and others had long borne grudges against Qian.

sentences.zh: 景泰八年正月壬午，亨與吉祥、有貞等既迎上皇復位，宣諭朝臣畢，即執謙與大學士王文下獄。

translations.literal: On renwu day in the first month of the eighth year of Jingtai, after Heng, Jixiang, Youzhen, and others had welcomed the former emperor's restoration, when the announcement to court ministers was finished they immediately seized Qian and Grand Secretary Wang Wen and sent them to prison.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day in the first month of Jingtai 8, after Heng, Jixiang, and Youzhen had restored the former emperor and addressed the court, they seized Qian and Grand Secretary Wang Wen and threw them into prison.

sentences.zh: 誣謙等與黃竑構邪議，更立東宮；

translations.literal: They falsely charged Qian and others with Huang Qiong in plotting heterodox opinions to change and establish the Eastern Palace;
translations.idiomatic: They accused Qian and others of plotting with Huang Qiong to install a new heir;

sentences.zh: 又與太監王誠、舒良、張永、王勤等謀迎立襄王子。

translations.literal: and further with eunuchs Wang Cheng, Shu Liang, Zhang Yong, Wang Qin, and others in plotting to welcome and establish the Prince of Xiang's son.
translations.idiomatic: and of conspiring with eunuchs Wang Cheng, Shu Liang, Zhang Yong, and Wang Qin to enthrone the Prince of Xiang's son.

sentences.zh: 亨等主其議，嗾言官上之。

translations.literal: Heng and others directed this accusation and incited remonstrating officials to submit it.
translations.idiomatic: Heng and his faction drove the case and incited censors to submit the charges.

sentences.zh: 都御史蕭惟禎定讞。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Xiao Weizhen fixed the verdict.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Xiao Weizhen pronounced sentence.

sentences.zh: 坐以謀逆，處極刑。

translations.literal: Convicted of plotting rebellion, they received the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: They were convicted of treason and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 文不勝誣，辯之疾，謙笑曰：「亨等意耳，辯何益？」

translations.literal: Wen could not bear the false charge and argued urgently; Qian smiled and said: "It is Heng and others' intent—what use is argument?"
translations.idiomatic: Wen could not bear the false charges and argued fiercely; Qian smiled and said, "This is Heng's doing—what good is argument?"

sentences.zh: 奏上，英宗尚猶豫曰：「于謙實有功。」

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Ying Emperor still hesitated, saying: "Yu Qian truly had merit."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached him, the Ying Emperor still hesitated: "Yu Qian truly served the realm well."

sentences.zh: 有貞進曰：「不殺于謙，此舉為無名。」

translations.literal: Youzhen advanced and said: "If Yu Qian is not killed, this undertaking has no name."
translations.idiomatic: Youzhen said, "If you do not kill Yu Qian, this restoration has no justification."

sentences.zh: 帝意遂決。

translations.literal: The emperor's intent was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 丙戌改元天順，丁亥棄謙市，籍其家，家戍邊。

translations.literal: On bingxu the reign title was changed to Tianshun; on dinghai Qian was abandoned to the market, his household registered and confiscated, and his family exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the reign was renamed Tianshun; on dinghai Qian was executed in the marketplace, his property confiscated, and his family sent to frontier exile.

sentences.zh: 遂溪教諭吾豫言謙罪當族，謙所薦舉諸文武大臣並應誅。

translations.literal: Suixi Instructor Wu Yu said Qian's crime deserved clan extermination and all civil and military grand ministers Qian had recommended should also be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yu, instructor at Suixi, said Qian's crime warranted extermination of his clan and that every civil and military official Qian had promoted should die as well.

sentences.zh: 部議持之而止。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberation held to this and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries debated the proposal and blocked it.

sentences.zh: 千戶白琦又請榜其罪，鏤板示天下，一時希旨取寵者，率以謙為口實。

translations.literal: Company Commander Bai Qi again requested posting his crimes, carving them on boards to show all under Heaven; for a time those currying favor by pleasing intent mostly took Qian as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Company commander Bai Qi asked that Qian's crimes be posted and carved on boards for all to see; for a time every sycophant found in Qian a convenient target.

sentences.zh: 謙自值也先之變，誓不與賊俱生。

translations.literal: From when Qian encountered Esen's crisis he swore not to live together with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: From the day of Esen's invasion Qian swore he would not live while the enemy survived.

sentences.zh: 嘗留宿直廬，不還私第。

translations.literal: He often lodged overnight in the duty hall and did not return to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: He often slept in his office and never went home.

sentences.zh: 素病痰，疾作，景帝遣興安、舒良更番往視。

translations.literal: He had long suffered from phlegm illness; when the illness flared the Jing Emperor sent Xing'an and Shu Liang in rotation to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered chronic phlegm disorder; when it flared the Jing Emperor sent Xing'an and Shu Liang in rotation to check on him.

sentences.zh: 聞其服用過薄，詔令上方制賜，至醯菜畢備。

translations.literal: Hearing his food and clothing were excessively spare, an edict ordered the imperial workshop to make gifts, down to vinegar and vegetables all complete.
translations.idiomatic: Learning how spare his fare was, the emperor ordered the imperial workshops to supply him—even vinegar and vegetables in full measure.

sentences.zh: 又親幸萬歲山，伐竹取瀝以賜。

translations.literal: He also personally visited Longevity Hill, cut bamboo and took the sap to bestow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself went to Longevity Hill, cut bamboo, and sent the sap as medicine.

sentences.zh: 或言寵謙太過，興安等曰：「彼日夜分國憂，不問家產，即彼去，令朝廷何處更得此人？」

translations.literal: Some said favoring Qian was excessive; Xing'an and others said: "He day and night shares the state's worry and does not inquire after household property—even if he left, where could the court find such a man again?"
translations.idiomatic: Some said the emperor favored Qian too much; Xing'an replied, "He shares the state's burdens day and night and never tends his own affairs—where will the court find another like him?"

sentences.zh: 及籍沒，家無餘資，獨正室鐍鑰甚固。

translations.literal: When his property was registered and confiscated, the household had no surplus funds; only the main chamber's lock and key were very secure.
translations.idiomatic: When his estate was seized, nothing remained but his main chamber, locked tight.

sentences.zh: 啟視，則上賜蟒衣、劍器也。

translations.literal: Opening to look, they were the imperial gifts of python robes and sword implements.
translations.idiomatic: Inside were only the python robes and swords the emperor had bestowed.

sentences.zh: 死之日，陰霾四合，天下冤之。

translations.literal: On the day of his death, dark clouds gathered from four sides; all under Heaven considered it wrongful.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died dark clouds closed in from every side; the realm mourned a great injustice.

sentences.zh: 指揮朵兒者，本出曹吉祥部下，以酒酹謙死所，慟哭。

translations.literal: Commander Duo'er, originally from Cao Jixiang's subordinates, poured wine at Qian's place of death and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Duo'er, once under Cao Jixiang, poured wine at the place of Qian's death and wept.

sentences.zh: 吉祥怒，抶之。

translations.literal: Jixiang was angry and flogged him.
translations.idiomatic: Jixiang had him beaten.

sentences.zh: 明日復酹奠如故。

translations.literal: The next day he again poured libation as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he returned and poured wine again.

sentences.zh: 都督同知陳逵感謙忠義，收遺骸殯之。

translations.literal: Vice Military Commissioner Chen Kui, moved by Qian's loyalty and righteousness, collected the remains and encoffined them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kui, vice military commissioner, moved by Qian's loyalty, gathered his remains and gave them burial.

sentences.zh: 踰年，歸葬杭州。

translations.literal: After more than a year, they were returned for burial in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later his body was brought home to Hangzhou for burial.

sentences.zh: 逵，六合人。

translations.literal: Kui was a man of Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kui came from Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 故舉將才，出李時勉門下者也。

translations.literal: He was formerly recommended for general talent and came from Li Shimian's school.
translations.idiomatic: He had been recommended as a military talent and had studied under Li Shimian.

sentences.zh: 皇太后初不知謙死，比聞，嗟悼累日。

translations.literal: The empress dowager at first did not know of Qian's death; when she heard, she sighed in grief for many days.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager had not known of Qian's death; when she learned of it she mourned for days.

sentences.zh: 英宗亦悔之。

translations.literal: The Ying Emperor also regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Ying Emperor, too, came to regret it.

sentences.zh: 謙既死，而亨党陳汝言代為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: After Qian died, Heng's partisan Chen Ruyan replaced him as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After Qian's death, Heng's follower Chen Ruyan became Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 未一年敗，贓累巨萬。

translations.literal: In less than a year he was ruined; embezzled goods accumulated to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was exposed; his embezzlements ran to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 帝召大臣入視，愀然曰：「于謙被遇景泰朝，死無餘資。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned grand ministers to view them and said mournfully: "Yu Qian was favored in the Jingtai court and died without surplus funds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned ministers to inspect the hoard and said bleakly, "Yu Qian served the Jingtai court honorably and died without a penny to his name.

sentences.zh: 汝言抑何多也！」

translations.literal: Ruyan—how much you have!"
translations.idiomatic: And you, Ruyan—how much you have amassed!"

sentences.zh: 亨俯首不能對。

translations.literal: Heng bowed his head and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Heng bowed his head in silence.

sentences.zh: 俄有邊警，帝憂形於色。

translations.literal: Soon there was a frontier alarm and worry showed on the emperor's face.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a frontier alarm came, and worry showed on the emperor's face.

sentences.zh: 恭順侯吳瑾侍，進曰：「使于謙在，當不令寇至此。」

translations.literal: Marquis of Gongshun Wu Jin attended and advanced, saying: "If Yu Qian were here, he would not have let the invaders reach this point."
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Wu Jin, attending him, said, "Had Yu Qian lived, the enemy would never have come this far."

sentences.zh: 帝為默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 是年，有貞為亨所中，戍金齒。

translations.literal: That year Youzhen was struck by Heng and was exiled to garrison at Jinchi.
translations.idiomatic: That year Youzhen was brought down by Heng and exiled to Jinchi.

sentences.zh: 又數年，亨亦下獄死，吉祥謀反族誅，謙事白。

translations.literal: Several years later Heng also entered prison and died; Jixiang plotted rebellion and his clan was executed; Qian's case was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later Heng died in prison; Jixiang rebelled and his clan was exterminated; Qian's case was cleared.

sentences.zh: 成化初，冕赦歸，上疏訟冤，得復官賜祭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, Mian was pardoned and returned, submitted a memorial to plead the injustice, and obtained restoration of office and bestowed sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua, Mian was pardoned and returned; he memorialized to clear his father's name and won restoration of rank and imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 誥曰：「當國家之多難，保社稷以無虞，惟公道之獨恃，為權奸所並嫉。

translations.literal: The patent of nobility said: "When the state had many hardships, he preserved the altars of state and grain without worry, relying alone on public principle, and was jointly envied by powerful traitors.
translations.idiomatic: The patent of nobility read: "In the realm's darkest hour he kept the altars secure, standing alone on public duty, and the powerful traitors destroyed him together.

sentences.zh: 在先帝已知其枉，而朕心實憐其忠。」

translations.literal: The former emperor already knew his wrong, and Our heart truly pities his loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: The former emperor knew he was wronged; We truly pity his loyalty."

sentences.zh: 天下傳誦焉。

translations.literal: All under Heaven transmitted and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: The words spread through the realm.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，用給事中孫需言，贈特進光祿大夫、柱國、太傅，諡肅湣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi, following Supervising Secretary Sun Xu's words, he was posthumously granted Special Advancement Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Pillar of the State, and Grand Tutor, with posthumous title Su Min.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 2, on supervising secretary Sun Xu's recommendation, he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Pillar of the State, and Grand Tutor, with the posthumous title Su Min.

sentences.zh: 賜祠於其墓曰「旌功」，有司歲時致祭。

translations.literal: A shrine was bestowed at his tomb called "Commending Merit," and the relevant offices offered sacrifices each year.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine called "Commending Merit" was built at his tomb, with annual sacrifices by the local authorities.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，改諡忠肅。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period the posthumous title was changed to Zhong Su.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli his posthumous title was changed to Zhong Su (Loyal and Stern).

sentences.zh: 杭州、河南、山西皆世奉祀不絕。

translations.literal: Hangzhou, Henan, and Shanxi all for generations maintained sacrifices without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou, Henan, and Shanxi have maintained his cult without interruption ever since.

sentences.zh: 子 冕

translations.literal: Son: Mian
translations.idiomatic: Son: Mian

sentences.zh: 冕，字景瞻，廕授副千戶，坐戍龍門。

translations.literal: Mian, styled Jingzhan, received yin privilege as Vice Company Commander and by conviction was exiled to garrison at Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, styled Jingzhan, inherited a vice company commandership but was exiled to Longmen when his father fell.

sentences.zh: 謙冤既雪，並復冕官。

translations.literal: After Qian's injustice was cleared, Mian's office was also restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian's name was cleared, Mian's rank was restored as well.

sentences.zh: 自陳不願武職，改兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: He himself stated he did not wish a military post and was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to leave the military service and was made a vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 居官有幹局，累遷至應天府尹。

translations.literal: In office he had administrative capacity and was repeatedly transferred up to Prefect of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: He proved capable in office and rose to prefect of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 致仕卒。

translations.literal: He retired from office and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and died.

sentences.zh: 無子，以族子允忠為後，世襲杭州衛副千戶，奉祠。

translations.literal: Having no son, he took clansman Yunzhong as heir, who hereditarily inherited Vice Company Commander of Hangzhou Guard and maintained the shrine cult.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son and adopted his clansman Yunzhong, who inherited the Hangzhou guard vice commandership and tended the shrine.

sentences.zh: 附 吳寧

translations.literal: Appended: Wu Ning
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Wu Ning

sentences.zh: 吳寧，字永清，歙人。

translations.literal: Wu Ning, styled Yongqing, was a man of She.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ning, styled Yongqing, came from She county.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年進士，除兵部主事。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Xuande, appointed Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Xuande 5 and was made a director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 正統中，再遷職方郎中。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong he was twice transferred to Bureau Director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengtong he rose twice to director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 郕王監國，謙薦擢本部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Cheng supervised the state, Qian recommended him for promotion to Right Vice Minister of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Cheng took charge of the realm, Qian recommended him as Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 謙禦寇城外，寧掌部事，命赴軍中議方略。

translations.literal: Qian resisted invaders outside the walls; Ning managed ministry affairs and was ordered to go to the army to deliberate strategy.
translations.idiomatic: While Qian fought outside the walls, Ning ran the ministry and was sent to the army to plan strategy.

sentences.zh: 比還，城門弗啟，寇騎充斥，寧立雨中指揮兵士，移時乃入。

translations.literal: When he returned, the gates were not opened and enemy horsemen filled the area; Ning stood in the rain directing soldiers, and only after some time entered.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the gates were still shut and enemy horsemen filled the streets; Ning stood in the rain directing troops for a long while before he could enter.

sentences.zh: 寇既退，畿民猶日數驚，相率南徙。

translations.literal: After the invaders retreated, capital-region commoners still were alarmed several times daily and led one another south in migration.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the enemy withdrew, people around the capital panicked daily and fled south in bands.

sentences.zh: 或議仍召勤王兵。

translations.literal: Some deliberated again summoning relief armies.
