translations.idiomatic: Some proposed summoning relief armies again.

sentences.zh: 寧曰：「是益之使驚也，莫若告捷四方，人心自定。」

translations.literal: Ning said: "This would increase and make them alarmed; better to announce victory to the four quarters—hearts will settle themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Ning said, "That would only spread panic. Better to announce victory to the four quarters—then minds will steady themselves."

sentences.zh: 因具奏行之。

translations.literal: He then fully memorialized and it was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized accordingly and the court acted on it.

sentences.zh: 景泰改元，以疾乞歸，後不復出。

translations.literal: When Jingtai changed the reign title, he begged return on account of illness and afterward did not emerge again.
translations.idiomatic: When the reign was renamed Jingtai he retired on grounds of illness and never served again.

sentences.zh: 家居三十餘年卒。

translations.literal: He dwelt at home more than thirty years and died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home more than thirty years and died.

sentences.zh: 寧方介有識鑒。

translations.literal: Ning was upright and had discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was upright and discerning.

sentences.zh: 嘗為謙擇婿，得千戶硃驥。

translations.literal: He once chose a son-in-law for Qian and obtained Company Commander Zhu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He once chose a son-in-law for Qian—the company commander Zhu Ji.

sentences.zh: 謙疑之，寧曰：「公他日當得其力。」

translations.literal: Qian doubted him; Ning said: "Your Excellency one day will obtain his strength."
translations.idiomatic: Qian was doubtful; Ning said, "You will need his strength one day."

sentences.zh: 謙被刑，驥果歸其喪，葬之。

translations.literal: When Qian suffered execution, Ji indeed returned his coffin and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian was executed, Ji did return his body and gave him burial.

sentences.zh: 驥自有傳。

translations.literal: Ji has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ji has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 附 王偉

translations.literal: Appended: Wang Wei
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Wang Wei

sentences.zh: 王偉，字士英，攸人。

translations.literal: Wang Wei, styled Shiying, was a man of You.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei, styled Shiying, came from You county.

sentences.zh: 年十四，隨父謫戍宣府。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he followed his father in exile to garrison at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he followed his father into exile at Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 宣宗巡邊，獻《安邊頌》，命補保安州學生。

translations.literal: When the Xuande Emperor toured the frontier he presented "Ode on Securing the Frontier" and was ordered to fill a vacancy as student at Bao'an Prefecture school.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuande Emperor toured the frontier he presented an "Ode on Securing the Frontier" and was enrolled as a student at Bao'an.

sentences.zh: 舉正統元年進士，改庶起士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: He passed jinshi in the first year of Zhengtong, was changed to Hanlin Bachelor, and appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Zhengtong 1, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was made a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，命行監察御史事，集民壯守廣平。

translations.literal: When the Ying Emperor went north on the hunt, he was ordered to perform supervising censor duties and gathered strong civilians to guard Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was captured in the north, he was assigned censorial duties and rallied militia to hold Guangping.

sentences.zh: 謙引為職方司郎中。

translations.literal: Qian brought him in as Bureau Director in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Qian brought him in as director in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 軍書填委，處分多中窾會，遂薦擢兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Military documents piled up; his dispositions mostly hit the vital point, and he was recommended for promotion to Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Military papers piled up; his dispositions usually hit the mark, and Qian recommended him as Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 出視邊，叛人小田兒為敵間，謙屬偉圖之。

translations.literal: Going out to inspect the frontier, the rebel Xiaotian'er served as enemy agent; Qian entrusted Wei to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: On frontier inspection he found the defector Xiaotian'er acting as an enemy agent; Qian charged Wei to deal with him.

sentences.zh: 會田兒隨貢使入，至陽和城，壯士從道旁突出，斷其頭去，使者不敢詰。

translations.literal: When Tian'er followed tribute envoys in and reached Yanghe city, stalwarts burst out from beside the road, cut off his head and left; the envoys did not dare inquire.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaotian'er entered with a tribute mission and reached Yanghe, braves leaped from the roadside and struck off his head; the envoys dared not protest.

sentences.zh: 偉喜任智數。

translations.literal: Wei delighted in employing stratagems and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Wei delighted in stratagem and cunning.

sentences.zh: 既為謙所引，恐嫉謙者目己為朋附，嘗密奏謙誤，冀自解。

translations.literal: Having been brought in by Qian, he feared those who envied Qian would view him as a partisan and once secretly memorialized Qian's errors, hoping to extricate himself.
translations.idiomatic: Having risen through Qian's patronage, he feared Qian's enemies would see him as a partisan; he once secretly reported Qian's faults, hoping to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 帝以其奏授謙，謙叩頭謝。

translations.literal: The emperor gave his memorial to Qian; Qian knocked his head and thanked.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor handed the memorial to Qian; Qian kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾自知卿，何謝為？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I myself know you—why thank?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I know you well—why thank me?"

sentences.zh: 謙出，偉問：「上與公何言？」

translations.literal: Qian exited; Wei asked: "What did His Majesty and Your Excellency say?"
translations.idiomatic: Qian left; Wei asked, "What did His Majesty say to you?"

sentences.zh: 謙笑曰：「我有失，望君面規我，何至爾邪？」

translations.literal: Qian smiled and said: "If I have faults, I hope you will face me and regulate me—how did it come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: Qian smiled: "If I err, tell me to my face—why go behind my back?"

sentences.zh: 出奏示之，偉大慚沮。

translations.literal: He produced the memorial and showed it; Wei was greatly ashamed and dejected.
translations.idiomatic: He showed Wei the memorial; Wei was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 然竟坐謙黨，罷歸。

translations.literal: Yet in the end he was convicted as Qian's partisan and dismissed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Qian fell he was dismissed as a partisan.

sentences.zh: 成化三年復官，請毀白琦所鏤板。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chenghua his office was restored; he requested destroying the carved boards Bai Qi had made.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 3 he was restored to office and asked that Bai Qi's carved libel boards be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 逾年，告病歸卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he reported illness, returned, and died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he retired on grounds of illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：于謙為巡撫時，聲績表著，卓然負經世之才。

translations.literal: The encomium says: When Yu Qian was grand coordinator, his reputation and achievements were outstanding, and he outstandingly bore talent for ordering the age.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: As grand coordinator Yu Qian's reputation and achievements were outstanding; he clearly possessed the talent to govern an age.

sentences.zh: 及時遘艱虞，繕兵固圉。

translations.literal: When the time encountered hardship and peril, he repaired arms and secured the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When crisis struck, he repaired the armies and secured the realm.

sentences.zh: 景帝既推心置腹，謙亦憂國忘家，身系安危，志存宗社，厥功偉矣。

translations.literal: The Jing Emperor had already opened his heart and placed his belly in trust; Qian also worried for the state and forgot his household, his person tied to security and peril, his will set on the ancestral altars and state—his achievement was great.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing Emperor trusted him utterly; Qian in turn forgot home for the state, tied his life to the realm's safety, and held the altars in his heart—his achievement was immense.

sentences.zh: 變起奪門，禍機猝發，徐、石之徒出力而擠之死，當時莫不稱冤。

translations.literal: Crisis arose from seizing the gate; disaster's mechanism burst forth suddenly; Xu, Shi, and their kind exerted force and squeezed him to death—all at the time called it wrongful.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup at the palace gate struck, disaster erupted in an instant; Xu, Shi, and their faction forced him to his death, and all who lived then called it injustice.

sentences.zh: 然有貞與亨、吉祥相繼得禍，皆不旋踵。

translations.literal: Yet Youzhen, Heng, and Jixiang in succession met calamity, all without turning the heel.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Youzhen, Heng, and Jixiang each met ruin in turn, almost before they could turn around.

sentences.zh: 而謙忠心義烈，與日月爭光，卒得復官賜恤。

translations.literal: While Qian's loyal heart and righteous fervor vied in brilliance with sun and moon, and in the end he obtained restoration of office and bestowed consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's loyal heart and righteous fervor shine with the sun and moon; in the end his rank was restored and imperial consolation granted.

sentences.zh: 公論久而後定，信夫。

translations.literal: Public opinion after long time then was settled—truly so.
translations.idiomatic: Public judgment takes time to settle—how true that is.
